checks.title: Checks
checks.subtitleEmpty: Nothing is being watched in this project yet
checks.subtitleOk_one: {count} check, everything is reporting on time
checks.subtitleOk_other: {count} checks, everything is reporting on time
checks.emptyBody: Create a check, then have your job call its ping URL when it runs — or add the Spring Boot starter or the Python library and every scheduled task will declare itself.
checks.truncated: This project has more checks than this table loads. Narrow the list with the search box, or the REST API returns them all.
checks.noMatchBody: Nothing here is called that, or is in that state. Clear the search to see them all.
checks.sourceAutoTip: Declared automatically by a client library
checks.sourceOrphanedTip: The client stopped declaring this job. History is kept; delete it when you are sure.
checkForm.name: Name
checkForm.periodHint: How often the job should report in
checkForm.graceHint: How late a run may be before you are alerted
checkForm.environmentHint: Optional — keeps staging and production apart
detail.pingHint: call it when the job finishes
detail.orphaned: — the client stopped reporting it {when}. History is kept until you delete it.
detail.noPingBody: The first call to the ping URL above will appear here within seconds.
detail.pingsTruncated: Showing the most recent {count} pings. Older ones are still in the database and the REST API returns them.
detail.noPingMatchBody: Nothing in this log says that. Clear the search to see them all.
detail.noIncidentBody: This job has never gone quiet.
detail.noIncidentMatchBody: Nothing here is in that state. Clear the search to see them all.
detail.rotateMessage: The URL for "{name}" stops working immediately. Any job still calling it will be reported as down until you update it. History and incidents are kept.
detail.rotated: New ping URL issued — update your jobs
detail.rotateFailed: Could not rotate the ping URL.
detail.deleteMessage: {pings} and {incidents} are destroyed with it. This cannot be undone.
detail.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the URL manually
channels.title: Alerting
channels.subtitle: Every enabled channel is notified when a check goes down, and again when it recovers.
channels.name: Name
channels.secretHint: Signs each payload with HMAC-SHA256 so you can verify it came from us
channels.emptyBody: Until one exists, SilenceWatch detects outages but has nobody to tell.
channels.added: Channel added — send a test to make sure it works
channels.testFailed: The test alert could not be delivered.
channels.deleteMessage: Alerts stop going to it immediately. Checks carry on being watched — if this is the only channel, nothing will be sent when one goes down.
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: All the settings for your account.
settings.projectsBody: Checks, channels and history all belong to a project. An account always has at least one.
settings.lastProjectTip: An account needs at least one project
settings.projectDeleteEmpty: This project has no checks. Deleting it cannot be undone.
settings.projectDeleteMessage_one: This deletes {count} check with every ping and incident recorded against it. It cannot be undone.
settings.projectDeleteMessage_other: This deletes {count} checks with every ping and incident recorded against them. It cannot be undone.
settings.keysBody: Used by the REST API and by the client starters. A key is scoped to this project and cannot create other keys.
settings.newKeyTitle: Copy this key now — it is never shown again.
settings.revokeMessage: Anything using this key stops working immediately — a starter holding it will fail to declare its jobs, and the checks it declared will go quiet. Revoking cannot be undone; issue a new key instead.
settings.passwordBody: Changing it signs you out of your other devices.
settings.securityBody: Who did what, kept for a year. Sign-ins and password changes are yours; key and channel changes belong to the project.
settings.noMatchBody: No activity says that. Clear the search to see everything again.
settings.dangerBody: Permanently delete your account and everything in it. This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.title: Delete your account?
deleteAccount.warning: Your account and all its data will be deleted immediately and for good. There is no way to get them back.
deleteAccount.scope: That includes {projects} and {checks}, with their ping history, incidents, API keys and alert channels.
deleteAccount.failed: The account could not be deleted
settings.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the text manually
stats.title: Instance statistics
stats.body: Figures for the whole application, shown to you alone as its administrator. Counts only: no account or check is named.
stats.accountsNote: All accounts, and how they grew over 30 days.
stats.subscriptionsNote: Paid, or a payment still being retried.
stats.emailsNote: Per day. Deliveries are kept 30 days; test alerts are not counted.
stats.activeNote: Signed in, or used, in the last 30 days.
stats.failedAlertsNote: Given up on after every retry. By day, then by channel type.
stats.refusedNote: By day, then why. The address refused is not kept.

settings.signInFailed: That did not work. Try again.
settings.passkeysBody: What you sign in with. Add one for each device you use, so that losing one never locks you out.
settings.passkeyRemoveBody: It will no longer sign you in. Make sure you can still get in some other way.
settings.passkeyLastNote: This is your only passkey. Add another before you remove it.
settings.recoveryBody: If you lose every passkey, a code gets you back in. Each works once.
settings.recoveryShownOnce: Save these now: they are not shown again, and the old ones no longer work.
settings.providerBody: You sign in with your Google or Microsoft account. There is nothing to set up here.
